title: Residency exception governance catalog
content:
Purpose: quick-reference governance catalog for residency exception requests and the minimum technical/audit controls we need to grant, monitor, and revoke them. This is a working doc (notes, checklist, TODOs) for eng-private-deployments + legal + security.

Background and scope:
- We frequently get requests where strict region pinning would block a customer use case (analytics pipelines, third-party vendor integration, legacy network constraints). Some of these are eligible for an exception if mitigations are in place.
- This catalog defines types of exceptions, required evidence, telemetry signals operators must see, SLA tradeoffs, and a lightweight decision authority model.
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC, on-prem) and Hosted with explicit contract clause. Not for ephemerally cached public model outputs unless customer explicitly requests residency waivers.

Exception types (quick taxonomy):
1) Temporary routing exception — timeboxed deviation to a neighboring region while capacity is provisioned.
2) Vendor-hosted storage exception — customer requests storing logs/attachments with third-party that is outside pinned region.
3) Hybrid compute exception — compute in one region, storage pinned to another (must be encrypted + minimal PHI).
4) Long-term negotiated exception — part of an enterprise contract with compensating controls (SLA adjustments, additional audits).

Minimum evidence checklist (must be attached in ticket):
- Business justification: short paragraph (product owner + customer contact).
- Legal attestation: note from customer legal (or Redwood legal) referencing jurisdictional acceptability.
- Data classification: per our DATA-CLASS categories (A/B/C/D) — list of fields/types involved.
- Architecture diagram: simplified flow (3 boxes max) that shows where data enters, where it residences, and encryption in transit/rest.
- Retention & delete policy: retention period and capability to delete on request.
- Audit sample: 3 rows of synthetic/sanitized evidence demonstrating how routing would be audited.
- Approved mitigations: e.g., tokenization, HSM/KMS usage, IP allowlist, contract addendum.

Decision authority & SLA:
- Minor temporary exceptions: product-eng lead + SRE oncall can approve (timebox <= 14 days).
- Vendor-storage & hybrid compute exceptions: legal + security + infra-eng must sign off (documented).
- Long-term negotiated exceptions: require Director-level approval (Product or Security) + contract amendment.

Operational telemetry & tagging (what the runtime must emit):
- residency.pin_decision: granted|denied
- residency.pin_reason: short code (TEMP_ROUTE, VENDOR_STORE, HYBRID_COMPUTE, CONTRACT_EX)
- residency.request_id: unique exception id (e.g., EX-2025-0001)
- residency.requester: email/team
- routing.x_region_pin: target-region-code (if any)
- audit_log_url: presigned S3/GCS URL or internal evidence pointer
- last_pin_modifier: user id that changed the pin state
- retention_profile: profile id (R1, R2, R3)
Notes on telemetry: these fields must be present in per-request traces for the initial 90 days after granting an exception, then for monthly samples for 2 years (or as contractually required).

Enforcement signals for operator consoles:
- Console view should show active exceptions with expiry, owner, data classes affected, and risk score (1-5).
- Alert rule: if a request is routed contrary to the exception policy (e.g., went to non-approved external vendor), page SRE + legal.

Audit evidence format (deliverable when granting exception):
1) A zipped bundle containing:
   - architecture-diagram.png or .svg
   - sanitized-sample-logs.csv (columns: timestamp, request_id, residency.tag, route, audit_flag)
   - legal-email.pdf or contract-excerpt.txt
   - retention_policy.md
2) Evidence retention timeframe: store the bundle for minimum 3 years for high-risk exceptions (DATA-C) and 7 years for PHI-equivalent per enterprise contracts.

Acceptance criteria (minimum) for granting:
- All checklist items present and pass a basic sanity review by infra-eng.
- Security reviews any cryptographic gaps (e.g., no plaintext transfer between regions).
- SRE confirms that telemetry will be emitted and can be queried by the compliance team.
- Legal confirms contractual language if >90 days or involves vendor storage.

Revocation & rollback playbook (operator steps):
- Precondition: notify customer 72h before planned revocation unless emergency.
- Step 0: create incident ticket and tag with EX-ID.
- Step 1: switch routing policy to fallback-model (region-owned) in canary mode 5% for 1 hour, monitor error and latency metrics.
- Step 2: increment to 25% for 30 min, then 100% if no regressions.
- Step 3: verify audit logs correspond and store final evidence bundle.
- Emergency revocation: if security/legal flags, immediately switch to deny-list routing and notify channel #security-incidents + legal@redwood.com.

Customer onboarding checklist (how to ask for an exception):
- Fill the Exception Request template (sample below) as a GitHub issue or Jira ticket with label residency-exception.
- Provide the architecture diagram and data classification matrix.
- Assign an internal product sponsor.
- Expect ~7–14 business day review for non-emergencies.

Exception Request Template (copyable):
- Title: [Customer] — Exception request — short reason
- Owner: customer contact + Redwood product sponsor
- Type: TEMP_ROUTE | VENDOR_STORE | HYBRID_COMPUTE | CONTRACT_EX
- Data classes affected: list (A/B/C/D)
- Timebox requested: start/end dates
- Business justification: 3–4 sentences
- Proposed mitigations: e.g., tokenization, additional encryption, signed NDA with vendor
- Attach: architecture diagram, legal attestation, retention policy, sanitized sample logs

Risk matrix (high level):
- Likelihood: Low/Medium/High (based on traffic volume & vendor exposure)
- Impact: Low/Medium/High (based on data classes exposed)
- Example: Vendor storage + DATA-C + high traffic => risk=High (need Director approval + quarterly audits)

Common pitfalls we've seen (notes to self):
- Requests arrive with vague architecture diagrams — push back immediately: must show the real network path.
- Customers often say "we'll pseudonymize later" — need to verify where that happens; if after region egress, it's insufficient.
- Telemetry fields missing in initial rollout; make telemetry gating part of approval checklist.

Operational queries & sample searches (for compliance team):
- List active exceptions: query by residency.pin_decision=granted AND expiry>now
- Sample trace for EX-id: filter traces where residency.request_id=EX-xxxx
- Monthly sampling job: pull first 1000 requests per exception and validate residency.tag present

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Retention windows: do we standardize to 3/5/7 years or defer to contract? (owner: Legal — Marisol)
- Telemetry storage limits: where do we store monthly samples (S3 vs internal archive)? (owner: Infra — Luca)
- Can we automate triage for TEMP_ROUTE exceptions via capacity forecasts? (owner: Product Ops — Tom)

Next steps and owners (short):
- Finalize acceptance criteria doc and convert to checklist in Jira PD-892 (Asha, due 2025-02-14).
- Add telemetry schema to schema-registry and create a Grafana dashboard prototype (Luca, due 2025-02-28).
- Legal to propose standard contract addendum template for long-term exceptions (Marisol, due 2025-03-07).

Slack channels & references:
- #eng-private-deployments (operational discussion)
- #security (for legal/security approvals)
- Confluence: RESIDENCY-EXCEPTIONS (master page)

Appendix: quick check example
- Example request: AcmeCorp needs temporary region fallback (eu-west -> eu-north) for 10 days while on-prem migration completes.
  - Data class: B (identifiers + telemetry)
  - Evidence provided: diagram, legal approval, sanitized-sample-logs.csv, retention_profile=R2
  - Decision: granted TEMP_ROUTE 2025-01-10 to 2025-01-20, approvers: infra-eng lead + SRE oncall.
  - Telemetry observed: residency.request_id=EX-2025-0007, residency.pin_decision=granted, routing.x_region_pin=eu-north

Notes: this doc is intentionally lightweight. Aim to convert key parts into a structured Confluence page and a Jira checklist that gates approvals. Keep comments here for quick iteration.

-- Asha (owner)
